patch_description: Replace the final zero-phase bilateral one-pole damper with a fixed-λ Whittaker–Henderson polish (second-order difference penalty). Rationale: the one-pole damper, even applied bilaterally, has a gently sloping passband that leaves residual ripple (slope_changes 20.4, false_reversals 14.2) while its exponential smearing contributes to the lag error (0.34). A second-order-difference Whittaker smoother has a much flatter passband and sharper stopband: it preserves genuine low-curvature trends nearly untouched while strongly suppressing high-curvature noise ripple, and being a global symmetric least-squares solve it adds zero phase delay. Critically, λ is held CONSTANT over the whole signal (uniform curvature penalty), so no segment gets a "curvature-relaxed" penalty through which noise leaks — the failure mode of previous adaptive-λ variants. λ is set from the residual ripple-to-noise ratio already available in the function: λ = clip(25·(r_std/σ_r)², 1, 200). When the Kalman/RTS output is already clean (r_std ≪ σ_r), λ is small and the signal passes nearly untouched (dynamics preserved); when ripple remains, λ grows and suppresses it. The system is pentadiagonal (I + λ·D2ᵀD2), solved in O(n) with scipy's banded symmetric Cholesky (`solveh_banded`, bandwidth 5), with a dense-solve fallback — preserving the 0.05s runtime budget. The polish is applied at full length BEFORE the final slice, so the `len(y) = n − window_size + 1` output contract is exactly preserved (the length-changing-post-smoother failure of Gen 23 is avoided).
